name: Supriya Lifescience Ltd
title: Supriya Lifescience Ltd - 543434 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 190 cr (+31% YoY) but EBITDA margin fell to 25% on water and solar-power costs; management reiterates Rs 1,000 cr and 33-35% margin guidance, with Rs 35 cr sales deferred and Rs 230-240 cr inventory to liquidate.

capex.quote: we have revisited our earlier plan to undertake the annual maintenance shutdown for Blocks A to D in August

triggers.label: Inventory Rs 230-240 cr to liquidate
triggers.quote: Somewhere around Rs. 230 crores to Rs. 240 crores. It is on the higher side.

triggers.label: Planned Q2 shutdown pushed back
triggers.quote: the planned shutdown will not happen in Quarter 2 anymore

triggers.label: EBITDA margin 25% vs 33-35% guide
triggers.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs. 47 crores, a decline of 8.1% year -on-year with EBITDA margins at 25%

triggers.label: Customs/export authorisation lapse
triggers.quote: there was a technical lapse of two days where there was a human oversight by the logistics department

summary.headline: Supriya Lifescience Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31% YoY to Rs 190 crore, but EBITDA fell 8.1% to Rs 47 crore (25% margin) on water and power disruptions.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 31% YoY to Rs 190 crore against Rs 145 crore in Q1 FY26, with management citing about Rs 35 crore of sales deferred by a water shortage at the Lote MIDC site. EBITDA fell 8.1% YoY to Rs 47 crore and margin was 25%, which management attributed to roughly Rs 10.5 crore of extra solvent and power costs, including about Rs 8 crore from a Maharashtra solar tariff change. PAT was Rs 24 crore (12.7% margin) versus Rs 35 crore a year earlier. Management reiterated the Rs 1,000 crore FY27 revenue goal and a 33-35% EBITDA margin guidance, while deferring the Q2 maintenance shutdown and flagging a customs/export documentation matter on one small consignment.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were 81% of Q1 FY27 revenue, split Asia 39%, Europe 35%, LATAM 20%. Management said over 80% of revenue comes from exports, with a large part from regulated markets.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Management cited a sequential improvement from four to five US DMFs filed, with customers starting validation volumes. North America is a small share, roughly 3% by an analyst's estimate.

segments.name: Backward integration
segments.commentary: 72% of total revenue is fully backward integrated, per management.

segments.name: Products launched in FY26
segments.commentary: Cardiovascular advanced intermediate (launched Q3 FY26) is commercialised; ADHD product scaling on LATAM and Europe demand; liquid anesthetic on steady monthly supplies.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue trajectory towards about Rs 1,000 crore is reiterated as on track, though growth is expected to be non-linear across quarters.
EBITDA margin guidance of 33-35% is maintained; management said margins should stay at 33-35% for at least the next three to four years.
Management expects to recover about Rs 25-30 crore of sales lost to the water disruption over coming quarters, and says the Q1 one-off cost will not recur in Q2.
Q2 FY27 planned annual maintenance shutdown for Blocks A to D is cancelled; replaced by smaller debottlenecking work, so Q2 production is not expected to be majorly affected.
Management said it expects about 20% CAGR, with potential to grow beyond 20% in coming years.
Ambernath depreciation is about Rs 14-15 crore; full-year overall depreciation is seen at Rs 35-40 crore.
capex_capacity: Patalganga land: all clearances received; Phase-1 capex about Rs 200 crore for API and utility blocks, with formulation blocks later in Phase-2; boundary wall construction has started.
Management expects about 40% completion around 2.5 years from acquisition, per MIDC requirements.
Block F at Lote: construction not yet started, expected to start in the next couple of quarters.
Ambernath: two anesthetic liquid inhalation products launched; EU GMP audit scheduled for second half of November 2026; CEP expected October-November 2026.
Contrast media (Iohexol) launch delayed about two quarters; now expected in H2 FY27 as R&D fine-tunes the technology.
Two ADHD product launches in the pipeline; SAP go-live expected in four to five months.
demand_pricing: Demand described as strong in Q1, but water shortage at Lote MIDC (Koyna river supply) cut production for about 15-20 days, deferring about Rs 35 crore of sales.
Company works on purchase-order basis and says it can pass on solvent, power and raw-material price increases to customers.
Solar tariff: Rs 4.5-5 crore retrospective charge, sub judice; management says the ToD-related and other increases will be passed through to customers.
Cardiovascular product: commercial-level volumes reached, but management said a larger contribution would take 9-12 months as customers complete qualification.
ATS-8 product: management reiterated 250 metric tonnes target over two years, not in the current year.

CMO/CDMO: term sheet close on a large anesthetic CDMO contract, expected to be announced next quarter; quality already approved; DSM vitamin ramp at near-peak volumes with a dedicated facility running.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Patalganga construction delayed, given Lote is full and greenfield pharma takes three to four years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said boundary-wall work has started and ground is broken. API blocks and utilities come first, as Lote is nearly capacity-exhausted; formulation blocks come in Phase-2. Ambernath is the formulation scale-up site.

qa_highlights.question: What is the customs/export issue and is there a provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a two-day lapse let an export authorisation expire before the shipping bill was raised. A new CBN export authorisation has been received, the matter is sub judice, and no provision has been made. Management said the consignment is small and limited to one shipment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost outlook for Q2 water and power, and is guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the water issue is resolved, the solar charge is largely retrospective, and price increases will be passed on. It reiterated FY27 guidance of close to Rs 1,000 crore revenue and 32-35% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambernath alone adds about Rs 14-15 crore; full-year depreciation is expected at about Rs 35-40 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How big is inventory and how will it unwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing inventory is about Rs 230-240 crore, built up for the planned shutdown. It will be liquidated over the next three to four quarters now that the shutdown is cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: Is there potential for growth above 20%, and what is the H2 ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 FY27 ramp-up will be much stronger than the current run rate, and growth beyond 20% is possible given CMO/CDMO, new products and capacity additions, subject to regulatory approvals.
